correctness.rationale: Let L=log n. Near each nondegenerate minimizer t_j, r(t_j+z/sqrt L)=r_*+r''(t_j)z²/(2L)+o(1/L) uniformly for bounded z. The centered exponential exceedance tails are sqrt L/(nK)e^{-y}exp[-r''(t_j)z²/(2r_*)](1+o(1)). Their rescaled mesh sqrt L/n gives the Gaussian integrals K_j, with off-valley rate gaps and local quadratic lower bounds dominating all tails. Hence sum of tails tends to e^{-y}, max tail tends to zero, and the exact maximum CDF product tends to exp(-e^{-y}). The exact joint winner-height density equals (r(i/n)/r_*) times the individual survival tail times the other-indices CDF product; summing over rescaled valley windows proves the factorized Gumbel/Gaussian mixture density. A no-escaped-mass bound closes the tightness step. Standard-library finite checks passed but are not used as an infinite proof. Assumptions and excluded boundary/flat cases are explicit.

value.rationale: The question extends a documented winner/argmaximum problem to natural competing hazard-rate valleys where the proportional-tail framework does not apply. It gives a complete, nontrivial joint limit for finitely many equally favorable wells, a universal -0.5 loglog n extreme-centering correction, a Gaussian location scale 1/sqrt(log n), quantitative inverse-sqrt-curvature selection frequencies, and asymptotic independence. These precise continuous-statistic facts are meaningful for extreme winner localization, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice or routine reparametrization. It does not claim a downstream theorem, rate of convergence, or generality beyond independent exponentials.
